images.note: Real, unaltered screenshot from Snowflake's own 'Getting Started with Snowflake' quickstart, showing a view's object detail page in Snowsight (View Details / Columns / Data Preview tabs). This is an ordinary, non-secure view (SEC_FILINGS_ATTRIBUTES_VIEW from the Cybersyn sample dataset) — captioned honestly as such. A secure view's detail page looks identical; this lesson's topic (hidden definition) isn't something a single screenshot can show, which the guide and caption both state plainly.

note: Only one real screenshot is used for this lesson, by design: no public screenshot source shows the SECURE-specific hiding behavior directly (it manifests as an absence of visible DDL to non-privileged roles, not a distinct screen). The lesson leans on three code slides (CREATE SECURE VIEW, SHOW VIEWS/ALTER VIEW SET SECURE, and the documented optimizer trade-off) instead of padding with unrelated or repeated screenshots, per SCREENSHOTS.md's guidance that a genuinely non-visual point should not be padded just to hit a screenshot count.
